title: find_ybegin() assumes caller passes line-boundary start offset but does not enforce it
description:
yenc.rs find_ybegin(body, start) assumes that 'start' is either 0 or an offset immediately following a \n. If called with a mid-line offset, the first iteration checks body[start..].starts_with(b'=ybegin ') at a non-line-boundary position, which could produce a false positive.

Currently all call sites pass either 0 (initial) or a post-\n position (after consuming a block), so the bug is latent. However the function's contract is not documented, and future callers could violate it silently.

Fix: add a debug_assert or document the precondition explicitly: 'start must be 0 or immediately after a \n in body'.
